title: Acute Compartment Syndrome
scenario: A 24-year-old male presents to the emergency department after a motorcycle crash with a closed midshaft tibia-fibula fracture of the right leg. A long-leg posterior splint was applied, and he is admitted for observation and pain control.

lines: 24-year-old male admitted after motorcycle crash with closed right tibia-fibula fracture. Long-leg posterior splint in place. Right foot warm, pink, with palpable dorsalis pedis pulse. Capillary refill < 3 seconds. Reports pain 6/10, relieved with elevation and ice. Wiggles toes on command. Alert and oriented x3.

Reports right leg pain now 9/10, described as deep, constant, and worsening despite two doses of oral oxycodone. Pain markedly increases with passive stretch of the toes. Right calf firm and tense to palpation. Numbness reported between first and second toes.
Provider notified of increasing pain, firmness, and paresthesia. Splint bivalved and elevation lowered to heart level per order. Compartment pressure measurement ordered.

Return from OR after emergent fasciotomy of the right leg. Wounds left open with sterile dressing. Right foot pink and warm, dorsalis pedis pulse palpable, capillary refill < 3 seconds. Reports pain 3/10. Sensation intact to light touch, moves toes freely.
Oxycodone 10 mg PO every 4 hours PRN pain
Ondansetron 4 mg IV every 6 hours PRN nausea
Position limb at heart level, do not elevate above the heart
Measure intracompartmental pressure and notify surgeon of results
Keep NPO and prepare for possible emergent fasciotomy
Administer supplemental oxygen; notify provider for urine output < 30 mL/hr

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: At 17:30 the nurse reassesses the client. Which 4 findings require immediate follow-up?

options.text: Pain on passive stretch of the toes
Numbness between the first and second toes

children.rationale: Escalating pain out of proportion, pain on passive stretch, a tense compartment, and paresthesia are the early hallmarks of acute compartment syndrome and demand urgent action. Brisk capillary refill and a low-grade temperature are not concerning.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each finding, click to specify whether it supports rising compartment pressure, muscle breakdown (rhabdomyolysis), or both. Each finding may support more than one.
children.rationale: Pain on passive stretch reflects ischemia from rising compartment pressure, while elevated CK and myoglobinuria reflect muscle necrosis. A tense, swollen compartment both raises pressure and reflects the injured, breaking-down muscle.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Complete the sentence. The nurse determines that the priority problem is {1}, and the priority immediate concern beyond the limb is {2}.

choices.text: impaired tissue perfusion of the right leg
acute pain related to the fracture
risk for infection at the fracture site

children.rationale: The limb is threatened by impaired perfusion from compartment syndrome, which must be relieved to prevent permanent damage. Muscle necrosis releases potassium, so hyperkalemia is the priority systemic threat.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each intervention, click to specify whether it is indicated or contraindicated for this client.

rows.text: Position the limb at heart level
Elevate the limb above the level of the heart
Apply ice packs to the compartment
Prepare the client for emergent fasciotomy

children.rationale: Loosening constricting dressings and keeping the limb at heart level preserve arterial inflow while relieving pressure; fasciotomy is the definitive treatment. Elevation above the heart and ice reduce arterial perfusion and worsen ischemia, so they are contraindicated.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: After the splint is bivalved and pressures are ordered, which actions should the nurse take now? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep the client NPO for possible surgery
Monitor serum potassium and urine output
Reapply and tighten the splint for stability
Massage the calf to improve circulation

children.rationale: Frequent neurovascular checks track the evolving ischemia, NPO status readies the client for emergent fasciotomy, and monitoring potassium and output detects rhabdomyolysis complications. Retightening the splint or massaging the limb would worsen compartment pressure and are unsafe.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Following the fasciotomy, which findings indicate that perfusion to the limb has been restored? Select all that apply.
children.rationale: Reduced pain, a palpable pulse, intact sensation, and brisk capillary refill all show restored perfusion after fasciotomy. Persistent numbness would signal ongoing nerve ischemia rather than improvement.
